newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeri industrial output grows first quarter 1997.
newsitem.headline: Azeri industrial output grows first quarter 1997.

text.p: Azerbaijan's industrial production grew for the first time in seven years in the first quarter of 1997, by an average monthly 1.1 percent year-on-year, deputy economy minister Oktai Akhverdiyev told Reuters.
"The growth of industrial...production this year is connected primarily with the macroeconomic stabilisation which began in the middle of 1996," he said.
Official figures show Azerbaijan's gross domestic product grew by one percent year on year in 1996 after peaking in 1988 and hitting rock bottom in 1995.
He said the activisation of the private sector played a positive role in the process, while foreign investment in the economy also increased.

"The share of foreign investment in the overall volume of capital investment in the first quarter of 1997 was 62 percent, which is 33 percent more than for the same period last year," Akhverdiyev said.

He said average monthly inflation in the first quarter of the year was 1.3 percent year-on-year. He predicted gross domestic product would grow by 4.5 to five percent year-on-year by the end of the first half of the year, and industrial production would grow by 1.5 to two percent year-on-year.
Inflation for the first half of the year would not be more than one percent, while the volume of investment would grow by 20 to 25 percent and wages would grow by 20 percent, he said.
Akhverdiyev said the decline in output would be reversed as major foreign investment projects kicked in. He said target oil production was cut by 100,000 tonnes to nine million tonnes for the year.
Fuel and energy account for 60 percent of total industrial output.
